structure: For each matrix type: listed_open is the list of orders in the range for which the sources named in listed_open_sources give no matrix, copied unchanged. since holds later statements about orders of that list, each with its orders, a status (board: this board holds a verified matrix of the order; reported: a matrix is reported in a source that is not peer reviewed), the keys of the sources in baselines/references.bib, and what was read or checked. open is listed_open without the orders of since: the orders for which none of the sources read gives or reports a matrix. Every other order in the range is known according to known_sources. The sources object records the version and date of each source and how it was read. Nothing here is a statement about priority, and an order is called open only relative to the sources named.

sage2026unknown.version: SageMath develop, commit 8de8dad7bcb38e1baa43508cbe944bf04a2d0401; the file was last changed on 2026-09-30
sage2026unknown.read: The module documentation and the lists unknown_hadamard and unknown_skew_hadamard in its doctest, which cover orders up to 1200.
sage2026unknown.pending: Pull requests sagemath/sage#43079 (opened 2026-10-28) and sagemath/sage#43184 (opened 2026-11-20) each change unknown_hadamard to the empty list. Both were open on 2026-11-22. Neither changes unknown_skew_hadamard.

cati2024database.read: Read in full from the TeX source. The open lists were recomputed from its tables of the least m with a matrix of order 2^m n known (Hadamard, odd n up to 2999; skew, odd n up to 999) and agree with the SageMath lists for every order up to 1200.

djokovic2023skew.read: Read in full from the TeX source. Its list of the odd v below 200 with skew order 4v undecided (89, 101, 107, 119, 149, 153, 167, 177, 179, 191, 193) agrees with the two sources above.

egan2026recent.read: Read in full from the TeX source. It states that a Hadamard matrix is known at every order below 2000 divisible by 4, that the smallest order with none known is 2396, and that the smallest order with no skew-Hadamard matrix known is 356.

epoch2026hadamard.read: Read in full. It states that a solution encoding Hadamard matrices of every admissible order up to 2000 at which none was known, among them 668, has been reported. It gives no matrix.

kishan2026hadamard.version: Repository commit d885022144ba6bf4efa8315e14871a3736947527, not peer reviewed
kishan2026hadamard.read: skew/476 of the same repository. Its four sequences are the board entry n119-f302cc45a2f83e60917b, which the board's verifier checks exactly.

kishan2026skew.version: Repository commit d885022144ba6bf4efa8315e14871a3736947527, not peer reviewed
kishan2026skew.read: skew/README.md read in full. The stored matrices of orders 476, 820, 836, 980, 1004, 1012, 1036, 1044, 1100, 1140 and 1148 were checked exactly on 2026-11-22 (entries 1 and -1, H H^T = nI, H + H^T = 2I). Order 996 has no stored matrix: its four sequences were placed in the Goethals-Seidel array over the cyclic group of order 249 and the result was checked in the same way.

since.note: Announced on 12 August 2026 by Alpöge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle, with eight larger orders, according to [@egan2026recent], whose authors state that they verified the matrices; see also [@epoch2026hadamard]. The matrices were not checked for this table.

Two verified quadruples with a skew block at n = 89, found on 2026-11-22. A search of the literature and public repositories on 2026-11-22 found no earlier skew-Hadamard matrix of order 356; this reports the search and does not claim priority.
A quadruple with a skew block at n = 119 from [@kishan2026hadamard], imported and verified on this board.
Matrices in [@kishan2026skew], a software repository that is not peer reviewed. Each was checked exactly on 2026-11-22; none is held on this board.

Twice the orders 356 and 476. The doubling construction stated in [@cati2024database] turns a skew-Hadamard matrix of order n into one of order 2n; applied to the matrices of this board it gives these two orders. No source read states them, and the doubled matrices are not held here.
